_title: 5 Blogs to Read Before You Travel Japan by Train — WoW Train · glosx.app
_desc: Five independent blogs that explain Japan’s trains clearly: Shinkansen fares and tickets, getting around Tokyo and Kyoto, and why Japanese rail works so well.
b1: 5 Blogs to Read Before You Travel Japan by Train
b2: By WoW Train · November 2026 · 6 min read
b3: Japan’s rail network is one of the best in the world, and also one of the most confusing on a first visit. These five blogs explain it better than anyone we know. We recommend them to our own readers all the time.
b5: The reference for travelling Japan without overspending. Their Shinkansen fare finder lets you check what a bullet train costs between two cities before you commit to a rail pass.
b8: Written by people who know Kyoto and the Kansai region in depth. Their step-by-step guide to buying Shinkansen tickets removes most of the stress from your first booking.
b9: Read: How to buy Shinkansen tickets
b11: The most detailed independent guide to Tokyo we know. Their post on navigating Japan’s trains, subways and stations is the one to read before you land.
b12: Read: Navigating Japan's trains, subways and stations
b14: Thoughtful guides to travelling Japan independently. Their overview of train travel in Japan explains passes, reservations and which trains to take, calmly and clearly.
b15: Read: Train travel in Japan
b17: Local insight into everyday Japan. Their piece on how Tokyo’s trains inspired a project back home is a lovely reminder of why rail here feels different.
b18: Read: How Tokyo trains inspired a project back home
b19: Need times for a specific trip? See Tokyo → Kyoto, Tokyo → Osaka and Kyoto → Himeji on WoW Train.
b20: Writing about one of these routes? Take our times with you
b21: Every route page on WoW Train has a block called “Add this route to your blog”: a small card with the route summary and, where we have the official timetable, first train, last train and trains per day. Enter your blog and your name, and you get a short code that shows the card in WordPress, Ghost or any editor, with times that update by themselves. It is free. Try it on Paris → Amsterdam or Tokyo → Kyoto, or find your route in the route index.
